target_customer: iPhone and Mac consumers who wanted to free device storage and keep photos and videos in the cloud
problem: Phone photo libraries filled device storage and existing cloud options like iCloud and Dropbox were clumsy or costly.
business_model: Freemium cloud storage subscription (5GB free, paid tiers for more)
product_category: Consumer cloud photo and video storage

founders.name: Jan Senderek
previous_startups: Popset (YC, shut down and pivoted into Loom)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists four founders. Loom grew out of Popset per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Nicolas Bös
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page, no details.

founders.name: Daniel Wagner
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page as technical founder.

founders.name: Philipp Wein
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page as design lead.

exit.reason: Service shut down May 16, 2014 and users moved to Dropbox Carousel

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable photo sync and storage at scale with a small team, plus a Mac and iOS client.

defensibility.rationale: Cloud photo storage had many entrants and users could switch easily; a 2015 essay argued such startups all died or sold.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dropbox bought Loom in April 2014 to build Carousel, then shut Carousel in 2016 (announced Dec 2015).

market_need_then: Phones were filling up with photos and reviewers compared Loom with Everpix and Picturelife as ways to free up storage; Dropbox later said photos drove storage demand.

rebrands.why: Team concluded it was solving the wrong problem with Popset and pivoted to cloud photo storage, per TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no source on the name or logo and only tech press launch coverage; unrelated to the later Loom video company of the same name.

pivots.to: Loom cloud photo storage and sync
pivots.why: Team realized they were solving the wrong problem with Popset (TechCrunch). Year inferred from Popset coverage in February 2012, not stated by the source.

outcome_analysis: Loom pivoted from Popset to cloud photo storage, raised about 1.3 million dollars in 2013 from Google Ventures and others, and sold to Dropbox in April 2014 when Dropbox launched Carousel. The service was shut down in May 2014 and users moved to Dropbox, so the exit was a product shutdown into an acquirer, which then closed Carousel itself.
notes: No company website listed (dead). Seed amount: TechCrunch says 1.3M, another outlet says 1.4M; recorded 1.3M. Everpix, Picturelife and Dropbox were compared with Loom in reviews, but those reviews are undated in my results and the Loom launch date is unclear, so no competitors are listed. Loom pivot date inferred. Not related to the later Loom video company.
